title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-10
korean_summary: 내일 핵심: 상사가 보낸 처우개선 대표 보고서 숫자 검토 후 점심 전 의견 회신, 본사 소방 안전 현황 11시까지 송부(기한 지남), 새 관리자 도착 픽업 확인·단기직 급여 지급일
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Tomorrow is Tuesday, November tenth. This is your English briefing for Tuesday.

Today was busy, and you closed many things. You sent the firewood report, the mending contract samples, and two reminders. Tomorrow, there is one new report for the CEO, one late report for head office, and a new manager arriving. Let's get ready together.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for tomorrow. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a short practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for tomorrow.
Number one. The report to the CEO about better working conditions.

What is it? This afternoon at four thirty, my director sent a report to a head office manager. You are in copy. The report is about improving pay and benefits for our workers. The goal is to stop people from leaving after Tet, and to fix our staff structure. It asks the CEO to approve three items. My director asked for a review of any additions or changes, and then a report to the CEO.

Why is it important? This report goes to the CEO. The numbers must match our real headcount and payroll data. It is also connected to the plan to add sewers before March, and to the HR manager's opinion on the thirteenth month salary. If the numbers are wrong, the CEO will ask, and my director will be in a hard position.

Your first action tomorrow. Open the PDF file first thing in the morning. Check each number against the headcount file and the October payroll. Then send your comments to a head office manager and my director before lunch.
Number two. The fire patch status report for the head office manager.

What is it? A head office manager asked every factory for its fire patch status. The deadline was today. At about three PM today, she sent a reminder. She said that every factory except one has not replied yet. Our sister factory sent its report this afternoon. In our sent mail, there is no fire patch report from our factory yet.

Why is it important? The deadline has passed. Head office is watching fire safety closely this month. The compliance officer already solved one outlet problem from the safety check. She told the head office manager the cause was a loose connection. So we are doing the work. We just need to send the report.

Your first action tomorrow. Get the check sheet from the maintenance leader by nine AM. Put it together with the stock that the compliance officer reported. Send the report to the head office manager by eleven AM, and say sorry for the delay.
Number three. The new manager arrives tomorrow.

What is it? A new foreign manager joins us. He lands tomorrow, Tuesday. Our driver will meet him at the airport and take him to the hotel. His first working day is Wednesday, November eleventh. The company car will pick him up at six thirty-five in the morning at the hotel.
Why is it important? First impressions matter. If the pickup goes wrong, it is a bad start. Also, his documents for work must be ready from day one.
Your first action tomorrow. Check his flight time in the morning. Confirm with the driver that he knows the time and the gate. In the afternoon, check that the new manager is safe at the hotel.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the stock count corrections from the warehouse staff. Today you sent your third reminder. None of the corrections from the last stock count are in the stock system yet. Items one and three were due on Saturday. You also asked for a photo of the book or the Excel file that shows the shared fabric by style. That photo is due tomorrow. You can say:
This is my last reminder. Please finish items one and three and send me the photo by noon today.

Second, the reply from the tax adviser about the transfer pricing file. Transfer pricing means the prices between our company and head office. The chief accountant sent your questions to the tax adviser today. The tax adviser said they will reply before November twelfth. You asked the chief accountant to share the reply with you by Friday. You can say:
Please forward the the tax adviser reply to me as soon as you get it.

Third, the shared folder from the CAD leader in the CAD room. Today the CAD leader said the CAD team made two new folders. One is for the plastic templates. One is for the cutting machine programs. He also asked the person in charge to copy the files. You can say:
Thank you for making the folders. Please tell me when all the files are copied, and I will check them.

Fourth, the quotations for the December electrical inspection. An inspection company sent two quotations today. One is for a full safety check. One is for a check every quarter. You asked the compliance officer to get quotations from two or three other companies too. You can say:
Please send me the other quotations by Friday, so we can compare them on the same basis.
Fifth, the pay day for short-term workers. Their salary is paid tomorrow, November tenth. Please check with accounting that the payment went out. You can say:
Could you confirm that the short-term salary was paid today?
Part three. Replies you owe.
The first reply is to a head office manager and my director about the CEO report. Your reply can start like this:
Thank you for the report. I checked the numbers against our headcount file. Here are two points I would like to adjust.
The second reply is to the head office manager about the fire patches. Your reply can start like this:
Dear Manager, sorry for the late reply. Please find attached our fire patch status and the purchase plan for the missing patches.
The third reply is to the compliance officer about the C C T V and storage hard drives. She asked for approval last Friday. It is still open. Your reply can start like this:
Before I approve, please send me the list of the drives, their condition, and the quotation.

The fourth reply is to the HR manager about the long-term worker list. Today she sent the production manager a list of workers with one to two years of service. This list may be useful for the CEO report. Your reply can start like this:
Thank you for the list. Could you also tell me how many of them may leave after Tet?
Part four. The schedule and deadlines.
Tomorrow, Tuesday. The new manager arrives. Short-term workers get paid. The warehouse photo is due. The fire patch report to the head office manager is already late.
Wednesday, November eleventh. The new manager's first working day. The accountant will send the new fire insurance proposal.
Thursday, November twelfth. The overtime report for next week. The tax adviser will reply about the transfer pricing file.
Friday, November thirteenth. The weekly cash report and the weekly outsourcing report. The chief accountant shares the the tax adviser reply.
One more piece of good news. The hanger line item is closed. My director said the two hanger lines already moved to our sister factory in April.
Part five. English review.
Let's review expressions from today's card, from last Friday, and from last week.

The first expression is "assess." It means to look at something carefully and judge its condition. For example, "Please assess the condition of each dummy and tell me if it needs a new cover." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please assess the condition of each machine.

The second expression is a pattern. "Someone will take over this, while you continue to do that." Use it when you split a job between two people. For example, "The CAD leader will take over checking the CAD machines, while you continue to handle quotations." Now say it with me.
One more time. The new manager will take over the training, while you continue to handle the reports.

The third expression is "For your reference, here is how we did it." Use it to share past examples. For example, "For your reference, here is how we sold the hanger lines to our sister factory in April." Now say it with me.
One more time. For your reference, here is how we checked the outlets last month.
Now from last Friday. The word is "prompt." It means fast and on time. For example, "Thank you for your prompt reply. The lists are very useful." Now say it with me.
One more time. Thank you for your prompt reply.
The next one from last Friday is a pattern. "Please do this by this time at the latest." For example, "Please send me the list by nine AM at the latest." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please send me the check sheet by nine AM at the latest.
And from last week. The word is "reconcile." It means to compare two sets of data and make them match. For example, "We will reconcile the system stock with the physical count." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please reconcile the report with the headcount file.

The next one is a pattern. "I was told that this, but that." Use it when what you heard is different from what you see. For example, "I was told that the request was submitted, but I do not see it on the list." Now say it with me.
One more time. I was told that the report was sent, but I cannot find it.
The last one is "I would appreciate it if you could." It is a polite way to ask. For example, "I would appreciate it if you could send the October list by Friday." Now say it with me.
One more time. I would appreciate it if you could check the numbers today.

One bonus word from today's card. The word is "pending." It means until something is decided. For example, "Pending the CEO's decision, please do not tell the workers about the new benefits." Now say it with me.
One more time. Pending our decision, please wait.
And "estimate." Here it is a noun. It means a rough number. For example, "Please give me an estimate of the total cost for one year." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please give me an estimate of the cost.
Part six. A short role-play.
The situation. It is Tuesday morning. You talk with my director about the CEO report.
Anthony: Good morning, Director. Do you have a minute? I read the report on working conditions.
Director: Good morning. Yes. What do you think?
Anthony: The direction is good. But I'd like to adjust two points before it goes to the CEO.
Director: OK. What are they?
Anthony: First, I reconciled the headcount in the report with our weekly file. One number is different. I will send you the correct one.
Director: Good. And the second?
Anthony: Second, the cost. I would appreciate it if we could add the total cost for one year. The CEO will ask about it.
Director: That makes sense. Can you add it?
Anthony: Yes. I'll get back to you on the cost by noon today.
Director: Thank you. Please send the final version to head office too.
Anthony: Sure. I will copy him.
Now let's repeat two key sentences.
I'd like to adjust two points before it goes to the CEO.
I'll get back to you on the cost by noon today.
Here is one more short role-play. You call the maintenance leader about the fire patch check sheet.
Anthony: Good morning. I need the fire patch check sheet this morning. Head office reminded us yesterday.
Maintenance leader: Good morning, Anthony. Sorry. The office and the dormitory are still not checked.
Anthony: I see. When will you be able to finish them?
Maintenance leader: We can finish by eight thirty.
Anthony: Good. Please send me the sheet by nine AM at the latest. I was told that some outlets were damaged. Is that right?
Maintenance leader: Yes. We replaced one outlet. It was a loose connection.
Anthony: Thank you for the prompt action. Going forward, please check every outlet once a month.
Maintenance leader: Understood.
Now let's repeat two key sentences.
When will you be able to finish them?
Please send me the sheet by nine AM at the latest.
Part seven. A short practice of key sentences.
Here are five sentences you will use tomorrow. Say each one after me.
I'd like to adjust two points in the report before it goes to the CEO.
Dear Manager, sorry for the late reply. Please find attached our fire patch status.
This is my last reminder. Please finish items one and three by noon today.
Please forward the the tax adviser reply to me as soon as you get it.
Welcome, and nice to meet you. I hope you had a good flight.

Now say them again, a little faster this time. First, the report. I'd like to adjust two points. Second, the fire patches. Dear Manager, sorry for the late reply. Third, the welcome. Welcome, and nice to meet you.
Part eight. The closing.

That's all for today. Let's say the one thing you must do tomorrow. Review the CEO report and send your comments to my director before lunch, and send the fire patch report to the head office manager by eleven AM. Also make sure the new manager gets to the hotel safely.
Have a good evening, Anthony. See you tomorrow morning.
